newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM CEO SEES CHANCE FOR BETTER 97 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: UPM CEO SEES CHANCE FOR BETTER 97 PROFIT.

text.p: Juha Niemela, CEO of Europe's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy, said on Thursday he saw a good possibility for better 1997 earnings, and the company's official forecast of a full-year profit on par with 1996 was on the cautious side.

"It is quite evident now that pulp prices have changed their direction and are rising. That gives a real impact on product prices," Niemela told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview. He added that demand was strong.

Asked whether this would boost the company's earnings, Niemela said: "There is a good possibility for that as well. But to be on the cautious side we see that we will reach about the same level as we did last year."
In a statement with its first-quarter results released earlier, UPM-Kymmene said it expected "earnings for 1997 to be around the same as in 1996."
Last year, it made profit before extraordinary items and tax of 3.6 billion markka and an operating profit of 5.6 billion.
UPM-Kymmene's first-quarter profit fell two percent to 1.35 billion markka.
"Surprises to the negative side are also possible, but not as likely as they are to the opposite direction," Niemela told RFTV.
"In some markets the picture is somewhat unclear like in wood-free papers lately ... but overall I think we are now clearly turning towards the better in most products," he said.
A "real change" in magazine paper prices, which already had moved up slightly, would take place from July onwards as many long-term delivery contracts would expire at end-June, he said.
Fine paper prices had been turbulent, including "some price deterioration recently", but the rise in pulp prices "will stop this development and turn it in the other direction," he added.
The market for sawn goods would remain firm for many quarters ahead, Niemela told RFTV.
Looking back at the beginning of this year, he said capacity utilisation had been "very high but prices in most cases fairly low, or very low."
Group net sales fell 1.4 percent to 13.1 billion markka in the first quarter.
